title: Breaking the ice: uncovering miPEP171b control of grapevine cold stress response
content: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small regulatory RNAs that control numerous biological processes, including plant development and responses to environmental cues. They are produced from primary miRNA transcripts (pri-miRNAs) and regulate gene expression through sequence complementarity, leading to target transcript cleavage or translational inhibition (Song et al. 2019). Although widely considered non-coding RNAs, pri-miRNAs may contain short open reading frames encoding regulatory peptides (miPEPs) which can establish a positive feedback loop by increasing the accumulation of the associated miRNA (Lauressergues et al. 2015). The importance of miPEPs in plant adaptation has also been shown in crops. In rice, miPEP156e enhances miR156 accumulation and represses its SQUAMOSA PROMOTER BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE (SPL) targets, improving cadmium tolerance (Lu et al. 2024), while miPEP172b increases miR172b accumulation and represses its target INDETERMINATE SPIKELET1 (IDS1), enhancing salt tolerance (Lu et al. 2025). Despite these promising examples, our understanding of the diversity and relevance of miPEPs in crop stress responses is still developing. Expanding their characterization across crop species and environmental conditions will help establish their broader relevance in plant stress adaptation.
